title: Lockless Circular Ring Buffer with TypedArrays
concept: Ring Buffer Head/Tail Pointers & Modulo Addressing
problemStatement: Implement `createCircularBuffer(capacity)` that manages a fixed-size byte buffer. Methods: `write(byte)` (returns false if full), `read()` (returns byte or null if empty), `isFull()`, and `isEmpty()`.
interviewTrap: In shared-memory multi-threaded Web Worker architectures, circular buffers prevent lock contention between audio/compute threads and the UI thread.

testCases.name: Writes and reads bytes in FIFO order
testCases.testFn: const ring = createCircularBuffer(4); ring.write(42); ring.write(84); return [ring.read(), ring.read()];

testCases.name: Detects full condition and rejects overflow writes
testCases.testFn: const ring = createCircularBuffer(2); ring.write(1); ring.write(2); return ring.write(3);

testCases.name: Wraps around head and tail pointers seamlessly
testCases.testFn: const ring = createCircularBuffer(2); ring.write(10); ring.write(20); ring.read(); ring.read(); ring.write(30); ring.write(40); return [ring.read(), ring.read()];

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: An ArrayBuffer is a contiguous chunk of raw heap memory. TypedArrays (Uint8Array, Int32Array) and DataViews provide structured lenses over the buffer. Endianness matters when parsing multi-byte integers across platforms.
